It is an approved implementation follow-up to Astra reviews, covering the **Mirket skills website**, documentation refresh, a candidate **0.4.0** catalog with exactly **25 native skills**—including the re-authored Equip skill and new Secure, Release, Migrate, Deploy, and Operate skills—lifecycle hooks, deterministic routing, architecture-record conventions, and cross-host integration reliability. The November 11, 2026 audit recorded findings only; the candidate source changes remain uncommitted and partly unverified in live hosts, and are not yet an installed, released, or deployed state.

## Mirket repository: approved implementation scope

The user approved this order:

On November 11, 2026, the user authorized expanding Mirket to 25 skills by adding **Secure, Release, Migrate, Deploy, and Operate**, extending existing skills, completing the audit follow-up, and updating the website and documentation.

## Mirket website and documentation work

The Mirket repository’s website work is intended to improve skills onboarding and documentation access. The homepage is simplified around a hero installer and packaged skills, uses the original Mirket logo for site chrome and the favicon, and places the Mirket mascot to the left of the hero title.

The reported local implementation removes the old workflow section and hero buttons, and provides copyable installation prompts and manual installation commands. Two independent Astra High reviews of the local website found and confirmed fixes for layout, navigation, and control issues, including a keyboard skip link, a full mobile skill index, and clearer installer labels with arrow-key navigation. The static build, responsive layout down to 320px, and diagram readability were verified successfully. *(REF-ID: `conversation:01a1c517-3c3f-7313-8a93-2858baddff8c`.)*

The website and documentation are built from repository content—packaged skill metadata powers homepage cards, each `SKILL.md` powers its detail page, and the repository guide is rendered on the site as well as remaining available on GitHub.

The Mirket website provides `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`, and structured data.

The Mirket website also added a three-second mascot wink loop as part of the public-facing product experience.

The Mirket website generates skill documentation and adjacent-skill navigation, supports source-aware Markdown links and responsive animated workflow diagrams with reduced-motion static presentation, and publishes canonical metadata, JSON-LD, `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`, `llms.txt`, and versioned 1200-by-630 social PNGs. Its documentation currently describes 28 indexable pages for the 25-skill catalog.

## Why the changes are being made

The Astra follow-up responds to review findings that could make Mirket unreliable or unnecessarily obstructive:

The Mirket Plan and Orchestrate guidance is being aligned so that substantial work or explicit planning requests trigger the planning process, while clear existing authorization to execute remains valid without treating an unapproved written plan as approved. The guidance also preserves root-controlled delegation, independent-review requirements, existing work, and questions about changes to outcomes, product decisions, or authorized scope.

The Mirket repository is re-authoring **Equip** because a tool, format, representation, library, abstraction, or workflow can function yet still be materially poor for the task. Equip should compare staying, adjusting, piloting, and switching using evidence about expected benefit and adoption cost; guide authorized acquisition and verification while preserving human control; and challenge the problem-solving approach as well as the instrument. The user-approved references include all 13 discussion scenarios, including tool selection before a method exists, evidence gaps, fragile workflows, repeated workarounds, unavailable tools and fallbacks, authorized setup and first verification, hidden privacy or security costs, and whether a failure warrants replacement. Examples include questioning XLSX instead of CSV or compact JSON for transfer, floating-point values for financial records, an opinionated tool for a highly custom solution, or an inferior library when a cleaner and more efficient alternative exists—even when keeping the current choice is ultimately best.

The approved direction is to add Secure, Release, Migrate, Deploy, and Operate where authorized; and extend existing skills such as Focus for evidence from shipped outcomes. Supporting skills should return evidence to one owner for each outcome.

## Related Mirket Audit revision

A closely related but separately named Mirket repository initiative revises **Mirket Audit** itself. Its purpose is to make audit coverage and conclusions appropriately rigorous across repositories of different sizes. The revised Audit skill is intended to:

- review **changes, plans, and explicitly scoped systems or repositories**;
- inspect manageable repositories fully and use a defensible, risk-based scope for large repositories;
- scale repository coverage to project size while reporting exclusions;
- distinguish **verified defects**, **supported risks**, and **material improvements**;
- seek independent review when warranted; and
- fix findings only when the request or prior instructions authorize fixes, preserving the read-only default otherwise.

This explains the audit follow-up’s emphasis on evidence, explicit scope, material improvements as well as defects, and authorization before changes. The Audit revision was recorded on **November 9, 2026** as a Mirket initiative to make audit coverage and conclusions appropriately rigorous across repositories of different sizes.

A separate Mirket 0.2.1 audit-repair result is also recorded as published, with its installed copy refreshed. That repair removed duplicate planning ledgers and repeated approval gates, resolved conflicting testing and delegation rules, corrected plan recovery, made plan-marker reads safe, fixed Codex patch delivery to the design detector, reduced prompt-hook text from 3,517 to 272 characters, and reduced active workflow entrypoints by 84%. This published audit-repair result is distinct from the Astra follow-up's latest local working-tree status.

The revised `plugins/mirket/skills/audit/SKILL.md` passed static metadata and link checks, but the changes were still uncommitted and behaviorally untested. This adds implementation-status evidence to the audit revision without treating static checks as proof of runtime behavior.

The audit and lifecycle workflow also addresses lifecycle reliability and operational safety while preserving the read-only default and requiring authorization before fixes.

## Current implementation state in Mirket

The Mirket website and source-backed documentation are implemented in the repository under `website` as a static export. The November 10, 2026 implementation used the original logo for site chrome and the favicon. The website provided keyboard skip navigation, a mobile skill index, and keyboard access to skill articles. Navigation was consistent across the Markdown guide, memory guide, and skill pages. The site was deployed on November 10, 2026, replacing its previous local-only status; public HTTPS behavior and browser smoke checks were verified.

The static build and responsive checks passed down to 320px; the workflow diagrams remain readable with corrected sizing and alignment, and the final homepage placement was verified. Website and documentation changes were committed and pushed to the Mirket repository's `main` branch on November 10, 2026.

All 56 Mirket tests passed, the static site built successfully, and browser checks passed for installer layout and documentation links.

Alongside the website and documentation work, the Mirket repository's release changes strengthened lifecycle behavior.

The Mirket repository's revised skills and lifecycle hooks address audit findings by using trusted staged-index checks through the system Git executable with a restricted environment, preserving quoted commit arguments, correcting Design and Imagine routing, making commit targets deterministic, surfacing the one-owner routing rule, and simplifying bounded integration handoffs. The lifecycle work now supports read-only Git previews, makes the extra final review opt-in through `MIRKET_FINAL_REVIEW=1`, and keeps lifecycle hooks distinct from skills: prompt guidance and cleanup review are provided, while live behavior depends on host support and hook trust. The pre-commit handling explicitly covers compound, `-a`, and path-based commits and fails closed when inspection is unsafe. Mirket hooks do not perform cleanup themselves; a neutral cleanup result does not authorize skipping cleanup.

Further Mirket skill revisions were handled in batches while preserving existing authored work and reconciling shared guidance. The Mirket repository re-authored **Equip** in `plugins/mirket/skills/equip` using all 13 user-approved scenarios and an explicit working-but-poor-fit trigger. Equip compares keeping, adjusting, piloting, and switching, and when a change is authorized it guides setup through a representative task check rather than treating installation as proof of fit. The remaining listed skill revisions—**Debug, Design, Focus, Imagine, Preflight, Refactor, and Test**—were handled through batched decisions that reconciled shared guidance, while live evaluation and some routing risks remain deferred or unverified pending live testing.

Astra High reviewed the Mirket repository and both existing test suites passed, but a focused check reproduced a false commit block when a quoted `|` was treated as a shell operator; routing risks remained unverified pending live testing. Synthetic hook checks passed, while the delivery hook had relied on shared Stop-continuation state and could add a continuation to simple responses. The recorded implementation status for this hook revision said the changes were uncommitted and not installed, and live Codex and Claude behavior remained unverified.

The Mirket repository is also hardening architecture and cross-host integration practices. Settled ADRs use the established `docs/decisions/` location; `plugins/mirket/skills/architect/SKILL.md` initializes that directory for the first settled ADR when it does not exist, while `.work/decisions/` is reserved for private notes and drafts. The initiative includes host-contract regression tests and a cross-host smoke matrix for integration reliability.

The November 11, 2026 audit recorded findings only: it made no production-configuration or repository-source change, made no external server request, and introduced no persistent configuration change. Separately, the Mirket working tree was dirty on November 11, with source plugin manifests identifying candidate version **0.4.0** and exactly 25 native skills; source instructions, routing, website, and installation documentation had been updated. These candidate changes remained uncommitted and not installed, so live activation, released behavior, semantic routing, and live-host behavior remained unverified. The active 0.3.0 plugin and global instructions lagged the candidate source, leaving some local routing fixes inactive.

Memory reliability is an identified Mirket implementation workstream rather than a completed fix. The work must preserve current working-tree revisions while correcting installer configuration preservation, canonicalizing or rejecting legacy project mappings so recall is not split across banks, sharing effective configuration resolution with runtime diagnostics, and adding freshness and recovery checks. Local tests passing does not establish correct installed guidance or host behavior.

The expanded Mirket catalog gives the five new skills distinct ownership boundaries: **Secure** handles security and privacy, **Release** prepares versioned releases, **Deploy** rolls them out, **Migrate** changes persistent state, and **Operate** maintains service health and recovery. The website and documentation present a 25-skill lifecycle example of **Release → Deploy → Operate → Focus**, with Focus also reviewing shipped outcomes.

body:
## Mirket repository: initiative summary

The **Mirket** project is hardening its routing and lifecycle hooks in response to review findings that made hook behavior silent, unreliable, or ambiguous. The initiative covers deterministic commit targets, read-only Git previews, opt-in final review, explicit one-owner routing, bounded integration handoffs, and the existing implementation in `plugins/mirket/hooks/cleanup.py` and `plugins/mirket/hooks/distill.py`.

The purpose is to make workspace-cleanup guardrails and lifecycle guidance more visible and dependable without discarding previously authored work or silently overriding a human decision. Mirket is also adding host-contract regressions, a cross-host smoke matrix, and architecture-decision documentation while deferring live skill evaluation until isolated validation is complete.

## What is being built or changed

For this initiative, the concrete changes concern Mirket's delivery and pre-commit behavior, routing, and lifecycle guidance—not a claim that the hooks can guarantee compliance by themselves. Commit targets are being made deterministic; `git commit --dry-run` previews remain read-only; an extra final review is opt-in; read-only audits are excluded from execution plans; each outcome has one owner with supporting skills returning evidence to that owner; and bounded root-integration fixes are permitted.

Mirket is also respecting existing ADR conventions and, when no convention exists, initializing `docs/decisions/` with the first settled architecture decision. The initiative adds host-contract regression tests and a cross-host smoke matrix to improve integration reliability.

The Distill skill was rewritten so the target agent performs authorized work first, skips routine narration, and leads with verified results. Its guidance runs at session start and on each prompt; turn-end guidance is integrated into Clean's existing review pass without requesting another continuation. The change is intended to reduce unnecessary communication overhead, although actual token savings were not measured.

Mirket's lifecycle coverage is being expanded to 25 native skills to close the post-implementation gap around release, rollback, operations, and learning from product use. The new skills have distinct ownership boundaries: Secure handles security and privacy, Release prepares versioned releases, Migrate changes persistent state, Deploy rolls releases out, and Operate maintains service health and recovery; Focus also gained a shipped-outcome review branch. Skill handoffs, source instructions, routing, the website, and documentation were updated to describe the expanded lifecycle.

## Delivery-hook behavior and constraints

Mirket uses lightweight Python hooks for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, and Bash PreToolUse events.

The working-tree hardening makes `cleanup.py` Stop-neutral by default; when `MIRKET_FINAL_REVIEW=1` and `stop_hook_active` is false, it requests one continuation. Mirket's `distill.py` now emits the one-owner rule and the exact routing-guide path `plugins/mirket/references/Routing.md` at SessionStart.

## Current state

The initiative remains **in progress** as a lifecycle-hook effort. On **November 10, 2026**, live hook behavior remained unverified.

The recorded validation status is:

The recorded validation status is:
- Live hook behavior remains unverified, and routing risks still require live testing.

In short, Mirket is tightening its lifecycle behavior. Live hook behavior remains unverified, and the required isolated validation and independent review are incomplete. Live skill evaluation remains deferred.

The lifecycle-hook work and live skill evaluation remain as recorded above.

An earlier snapshot recorded lifecycle-hook changes as committed and installed on November 9, 2026. By November 10, 2026, the current Mirket hardening changes were instead uncommitted and undeployed; this later working-tree state does not replace the historical record of the earlier snapshot.

Mirket subsequently released versions 0.2.0 and 0.2.1 with expanded Design guidance, improved setup and documentation, followed by version 0.3.0 with revised Equip and Distill capabilities on November 10–11, 2026. These releases mark successive public iterations of Mirket's guidance and lifecycle-related functionality.

On November 10, 2026, Mirket skills were revised with stronger lifecycle hooks, corrected Design and Imagine routing, narrower approval and handoff gates, and simpler routine replies and small plans. A focused check reproduced a false commit block when a quoted `|` was treated as a shell operator, and the revisions addressed the related hook, routing, approval, and handoff findings; both existing test suites passed.

The current Mirket working tree contains the first ADR under `docs/decisions/`, deterministic-routing and preview changes, revised Stop and SessionStart behavior, and candidate version 0.4.0 source manifests with exactly 25 native skills, including Secure, Release, Migrate, Deploy, and Operate. Source instructions, routing, the website, and installation documentation were updated. These changes remain uncommitted and undeployed; the candidate state is not a claim of publication or production deployment, live hook behavior remains unverified, and live skill evaluation must remain deferred.

## Source attribution

These decisions and status notes belong to the **Mirket** project. The implementation location named by the project is `plugins/mirket/hooks/cleanup.py`. The detailed review rationale is recorded under **REF-ID: `conversation:01a1bb84-4822-7903-a68a-ab67584fa15c`**.

The newer routing and lifecycle findings are attributed to the **Mirket** repository and to the review and discussion recorded under **REF-ID: `conversation:01a1c517-3c3f-7313-8a93-2858baddff8c`**; the implementation paths named by those sources are `plugins/mirket/hooks/cleanup.py`, `plugins/mirket/hooks/distill.py`, and `plugins/mirket/references/Routing.md`.

body:
The **Mirket Hindsight** initiative, recorded on **November 10–11, 2026**, is intended to make Hindsight’s routing, recall, auditability, installation behavior, and readiness checks reliable without destructive changes to historical knowledge or existing working-tree revisions. The work belongs to the Mirket repository/project; the retrieved sources do not identify a separate repository implementing this initiative. Earlier validation reported the Mirket integration working across hooks, interactive MCP, surveys, backfill routing, linked-worktree isolation, and verified coverage and freshness checks. The latest read-only audit, however, reproduced a linked-worktree bank split and found that rewiring could drop effective memory settings; live activation, released behavior, and comprehensive host coverage remain unverified. That audit recorded findings only and changed no production configuration or repository source.

## What Mirket Hindsight is changing

- **Unify bank routing, while fixing the remaining migration defect.** Mirket uses the project registry for Codex hooks, interactive MCP, and surveys. The intended routing unit is the canonical project directory: Git subdirectories and linked worktrees should resolve to the same main project, while non-Git sessions retain their original directory. The registry provides directory-based bank isolation by resolving canonical project identities, sharing banks across subdirectories and linked worktrees, and assigning stable unique hash-based bank IDs to unmapped roots; compatible explicit mappings are preserved while conflicting aliases and duplicate banks are rejected. Repository basenames alone cannot merge unrelated projects. Durable session-to-project bindings can be recovered from verified transcript metadata when a temporary marker is absent. The MCP bank is selected at session startup, so switching projects during a session skips memory rather than mixing projects. The November 11 read-only audit reproduced a defect in canonical bank migration: a linked-worktree path received a fresh bank instead of reusing the existing mapped bank, splitting subsequent recall without deleting the original memory. This migration behavior still needs correction and verification.

The rationale is that reliable Hindsight behavior requires more than a healthy background process: it must capture the right fact in the right bank, retrieve it in the relevant later context, exclude unrelated same-named projects, recover after resume, and report whether the result is actually fresh and covered.

- **Make Hindsight opt-in and installation-safe.** Mirket’s setup prompt asks whether to install local Hindsight or use Mirket without it, and waits for explicit confirmation before changing memory settings. The Hindsight opt-in guidance is reflected in the documentation and README, with setup prompts aligned to that guidance.

- **Make routing state safe and reproducible.** Hook events retain their initial session binding, and the MCP server resolves its bank at startup. Reproducible wiring and resume behavior must also preserve effective memory configuration: the audit found that rewiring can replace an upstream MCP registration with a new environment while dropping recognized settings, so existing effective settings must be preserved or unsupported custom entries must be rejected before rewiring.

- **Harden routing and lifecycle handoffs.** The Mirket repository/project is also making commit targets deterministic, offering read-only previews before Git changes, making the extra final review opt-in, surfacing the one-owner routing rule, and simplifying bounded integration handoffs. These changes implement the two Astra reviewers' findings and strengthen routing and lifecycle reliability without adding ambiguity about ownership.

## Acceptance test and audit scope

The Mirket repository added `memory/doctor.py` and wired installation with `python3 -B memory/install.py --wire`.

The Mirket repository/project is adding host-contract regressions and a cross-host smoke matrix to the reliability checks. Its architecture documentation follows existing ADR conventions; when no convention exists, Mirket initializes `docs/decisions` with the first settled architecture decision.

The Mirket reliability requirements include preserving existing working-tree revisions; fixing memory-configuration preservation and canonical-bank migration; making diagnostics reflect effective state; and checking freshness and recovery explicitly rather than claiming instantaneous memory consistency. Validation is expected to cover the package, installed guidance, and host behavior. Installation guidance, the website, and project documentation must remain synchronized with the implementation.

## Why the initiative was needed

The memory records identify several reliability problems:

- Hindsight had a **cross-session memory split**: two older banks contained survey findings that were absent from the active bank.

The initiative therefore emphasizes source recall for fresh facts, preservation of legacy banks, and separate readiness/coverage/freshness validation.

## Current state of Mirket Hindsight

As of **November 10, 2026**, the Mirket repository/project had a live, functioning Hindsight integration: Codex hooks, interactive MCP, background surveys, and backfill routing used the same project bank; linked worktrees resolved to that bank; and unrelated repositories with the same name were rejected. Mirket also had `memory/doctor.py` in place and installation wired with `python3 -B memory/install.py --wire`.

The active Mirket bank had separately verified readiness, coverage, and page-first recall freshness at the time of the earlier final check. Legacy banks remained preserved rather than being rewritten.

Thus, the current state is best described as **the Mirket implementation is substantially established but not fully reliable yet**: routing, capture, page-first recall, and doctor-based coverage/freshness checks functioned in the earlier recorded validation, and the active Hindsight bank is `coding-agent::desktop-skills`. A later reinstall and wiring check preserved the existing bank and confirmed project-page retrieval and past-chat recall, while capture of a new chat was not tested in that check. The November 11 read-only audit then reproduced a linked-worktree bank split and found that rewiring can lose effective settings. Live activation, released behavior, and comprehensive current survey or conversation coverage remain unverified; the audit changed no repository source or production configuration.

The latest implementation was captured in the active Mirket bank's transcript, recalled successfully, and recovered into the initiative knowledge page without overwriting legacy history.

The live Mirket setup also recovered two archived chats and all four survey documents without overwriting legacy history; the doctor found all five main Codex sessions in the active bank. All four verified survey findings were updated against the clean repository state.

A completed survey receipt was recorded against clean committed Mirket HEAD `8a05fdc`.

body:
## Mirket project — Adapt skill initiative

The Mirket project is defining a revision of the **Mirket Adapt skill** and hardening its related routing and lifecycle hooks. The initiative was recorded on **Monday, November 9, 2026**, and is described as an effort to align Adapt with the user's guided decisions about context handling, investigation scope, reporting, memory freshness, authorized follow-up fixes, deterministic routing, and reliable cross-host integration.

## What is being changed

The revised Adapt skill is intended to:

- **Orient when relevant context is missing or stale.** Adapt should first establish the necessary context instead of proceeding as though missing or outdated information were reliable.
- **Investigate only enough for the requested scope and risks.** The investigation should be proportionate to what was requested and to the risks involved, rather than expanding unnecessarily.
- **Report findings when requested or when they are material to a decision.** Findings do not need to be reported indiscriminately, but they should be surfaced when the user asks for them or when they could materially affect a decision.
- **Use relevant authorized memory while checking decision-affecting staleness.** Adapt should use memory that is relevant and authorized, while checking whether stale information could affect the decision at hand.
- **Continue directly to separately authorized fixes after read-only orientation.** Orientation is not meant to create an unnecessary approval gate: once the read-only orientation is complete, Adapt should proceed directly to fixes that were separately authorized.
- **Strengthen lifecycle behavior and audit compliance.** The Mirket project's November 10, 2026 revision addressed audit findings by correcting Design and Imagine routing, narrowing approval and handoff gates, and simplifying routine replies and small plans while preserving the revised lifecycle behavior.

- **Preserve authored work and establish a visible baseline.** Mirket skill redesigns should preserve existing authored work, reconcile shared guidance, and make the baseline visible while revising the skills.

- **Harden routing, lifecycle hooks, and integration reliability.** The Mirket project is making commit targets deterministic, enabling read-only Git previews, making the extra final review opt-in, surfacing the one-owner routing rule, and simplifying bounded integration handoffs. It is also respecting existing ADR conventions, initializing `docs/decisions` for the first settled architecture decision when no convention exists, adding host contract regression tests, and creating a cross-host smoke matrix.

- **Expand the skill catalog and close post-implementation lifecycle gaps.** On **November 11, 2026**, the user authorized Mirket to add **Secure, Release, Migrate, Deploy, and Operate**, extend existing skills, complete the audit follow-up, and update the website and documentation. The Mirket repository's **0.4.0 candidate** now contains exactly **25 native skills**. The five additions have distinct ownership boundaries: Secure handles security and privacy, Release prepares versioned releases, Deploy rolls them out, Migrate changes persistent state, and Operate maintains service health and recovery. Focus also gained a shipped-outcome review branch, and the website and documentation present a **Release → Deploy → Operate → Focus** lifecycle example.

- **Make memory reliability and verification explicit.** Mirket's memory work must preserve existing working-tree revisions while fixing configuration preservation, canonical memory-bank migration, effective diagnostics, and explicit freshness and recovery checks. Validation must cover the package, installed guidance, and host behavior without claiming impossible instantaneous memory consistency.

## Why it is being changed

The stated purpose is to make Adapt follow the user's guided decisions about when context must be established, how far investigation should go, when findings matter, how memory freshness affects decisions, and how authorized fixes should follow an orientation phase. In particular, the design separates **read-only orientation** from execution while preserving the ability to continue directly into fixes that already have separate authorization.

## Current state

The project memory initially recorded this as a **new initiative**. A coding agent reported revising the **Mirket Adapt skill**, and static checks for the Adapt revision passed. The Mirket **0.2.1** release was prepared by bumping both plugin manifests from 0.2.0 to 0.2.1; all 53 repository tests passed at that stage. On **November 10, 2026**, the Mirket project also recorded broader skill and lifecycle-hook revisions addressing audit findings in routing, approval, handoff, and routine-response behavior. Earlier Mirket validation then recorded all **56** tests passing. The project progressed through releases **0.2.0**, **0.2.1**, and **0.3.0** between November 10 and 11, 2026: 0.2.0 expanded Design guidance, 0.2.1 improved setup and documentation, and 0.3.0 revised Equip and Distill. As of **November 11, 2026**, the working tree contains a **0.4.0 candidate** with exactly 25 native skills; source instructions, routing, website content, and installation documentation were updated for that candidate. The working tree is dirty, and this candidate state is not a claim of a commit, publication, or production deployment.

As of **November 11, 2026**, Mirket's lifecycle hooks were recorded as Python 3.8+ scripts with stronger lifecycle guidance, corrected Design-to-Imagine routing, and simplified bounded integration handoffs. Mirket will add host contract regression tests and a cross-host smoke matrix for integration reliability; these additions are planned rather than recorded as completed.

As of **November 11, 2026**, Mirket's working tree contains exactly **25 native skills**. The five newly implemented skills are **Secure, Release, Migrate, Deploy, and Operate**, with distinct ownership boundaries for security and privacy, versioned release preparation, rollout, persistent-state changes, and service health and recovery. Focus also gained a shipped-outcome review branch. A repository review covered natively authored skills, skill wiring, guidance quality, lifecycle coverage, hooks, Global Instructions enforcement, and simplification opportunities; source instructions, routing, the website, and installation documentation were updated as part of this 0.4.0 candidate work.

The November 11 memory audit identified reproducible reliability defects involving preservation of upstream memory configuration, canonicalization of legacy worktree mappings, and diagnostics using effective configuration. The required fixes and validation were defined, but the audit follow-up itself recorded findings only: no repository source fix or persistent configuration change was made, and related working-tree changes remained uncommitted and undeployed.

## Scope and attribution

All facts above belong to the **Mirket project** and specifically its **Mirket Adapt skill**. No external tools, libraries, services, dependency repositories, commit identifiers, or deployment details are included because they are outside the requested project's codebase scope.

body:
## Summary

The **Mirket Architect skill** initiative belongs to the **Mirket project/repository**. It is a revision intended to improve how the skill handles and documents consequential architectural choices in both new and existing systems. The initiative was established on **November 9, 2026**.

## What is being built or changed

The revised Architect skill is intended to:

- Handle **consequential technical choices** and explicit architecture requests in new or existing systems, using the available evidence from different sources.
- Keep routine decisions within already granted authority, while escalating decisions involving material impacts on **product, cost, security, and operations** to the user.
- Record each architectural decision **after the decision is made**; respect existing ADR conventions and initialize `docs/decisions` for the first settled architecture decision when no convention exists.
- Use diagrams when they are useful, particularly to clarify architectural boundaries, flows, or trade-offs.
- Research external technologies, patterns, or other options only when that research could materially affect the architectural choice.

## Summary

The **Mirket Audit** initiative in the **nazmirket/skills** repository, initially recorded for **Monday, November 9, 2026**, is revising the Audit skill so its audits are broader, more rigorously scoped, and clearer about the strength and type of each conclusion. The stated reason is to make Audit coverage and conclusions appropriately rigorous across repositories of different sizes. By **November 11, 2026**, the revision was part of an authorized follow-up accompanying the repository's expansion to a 25-skill catalog, with source guidance, routing, website, and documentation updated in the same working tree. The initial skill changes passed metadata and link checks, but the available evidence still does not establish live behavioral verification of the revised Audit skill.

## Mirket Audit: planned changes

- Expand Audit beyond defects in the current implementation to cover **changes, plans, and explicitly scoped systems or repositories**.
- Scale repository coverage to repository size:
  - inspect **manageable repositories fully**;
  - choose a **defensible risk-based scope** for large repositories;
  - report **repository exclusions**.
- Distinguish among:
  - **verified defects**;
  - **supported risks**; and
  - **material improvements**.
- Seek **independence when warranted**.
- Preserve the **read-only default** and fix issues **only when authorized**.

The consolidated observation specifically confirms that the revised Mirket Audit skill is intended to report **material improvements in addition to verified defects and supported risks**.

- Address **lifecycle reliability and operational safety** in the revised Mirket Audit and lifecycle workflow, including:
  - deterministic commit targets;
  - read-only Git previews;
  - making extra final review opt-in;
  - surfacing and enforcing the **one-owner-per-outcome** routing rule;
  - excluding read-only audits from execution plans; and
  - permitting bounded root integration fixes.

## Why it is being changed

The initiative’s recorded rationale is: **“To make Mirket Audit coverage and conclusions appropriately rigorous across repositories of different sizes.”** The planned scope and evidence distinctions address the risk that one audit method would either examine small repositories too narrowly or treat large repositories as though full inspection were practical. Separating verified defects, supported risks, and material improvements is intended to make the audit’s conclusions more precise rather than presenting all findings as the same kind of problem.

A related Mirket project initiative is hardening routing and lifecycle hooks to implement findings from the **Astra reviewers** and strengthen routing, lifecycle, architecture documentation, and cross-host integration reliability. It also respects existing ADR conventions and initializes `docs/decisions` for the first settled architecture decision when no convention exists.

## Current state

The project memory records the initial Mirket Audit revision as a **new initiative** retained at **2026-11-09 20:47**. An agent reported revising the Mirket project's `plugins/mirket/skills/audit/SKILL.md` to add repository-audit coverage, strengthen plan review, separate confirmed defects, supported risks, and material improvements, report repository exclusions, require authorization before fixes, and preserve the read-only default. Metadata and links passed static checks. The planned verification includes skill scenario checks and independent review. A later project observation records all **56** Mirket tests passing. These project-level test results do not by themselves establish live behavioral verification of the revised Audit skill.

The Audit sources do not name a more specific repository than the Mirket Audit/project context itself, so no narrower repository attribution is available for these changes.

A related **Mirket Critique** revision also updated the Audit wording.

Related Mirket lifecycle-hook hardening changes currently make commit targets deterministic, keep `git commit --dry-run` previews read-only, make extra final review opt-in, enforce one owner per outcome, exclude read-only audits from execution plans, and permit bounded root integration fixes. The first ADR was created under `docs/decisions/`; these changes remained **uncommitted and undeployed**. The initiative also includes host-contract regressions and a cross-host smoke matrix.

As of **November 11, 2026**, the **nazmirket/skills** working tree had advanced to a candidate **0.4.0** source state with exactly **25 native skills**, adding Secure, Release, Migrate, Deploy, and Operate while extending existing skills. The user-authorized work included completing the Audit follow-up and updating the repository's source instructions, routing, website, and documentation. This establishes that the surrounding catalog and follow-up work progressed, but it does not by itself establish live behavioral verification of the revised Mirket Audit skill.

## Initiative summary

The **Mirket** repository’s “Revise Mirket Author skill” initiative broadened Author from a narrower writing workflow to user-facing written communication. Its implementation uses a lightweight combined **Author and Distill** pass for Author-owned work: Author handles documents, substantive product copy, and issue triage, while Distill handles routine responses and supplies additional assessment and refinement where needed.

The reason for the change is to improve how Mirket produces and checks user-facing communication. The revised workflow adapts the **audience and format to the context**, asks when a choice could materially change the result, verifies **material claims and artifacts according to risk**, labels uncertainty when verification is not possible, and uses rendered-layout inspection where relevant. It retains **authorized issue triage** rather than dropping that existing capability. The change makes the settled Author policy explicit while preserving the limitation that a prompt hook can request skill use but cannot guarantee model compliance.

## What was changed in the Mirket repository

The recorded implementation updated all of the following within Mirket:

- `plugins/mirket/skills/author/SKILL.md`
- the existing prompt hook
- both instruction sources

The prompt hook and instruction sources were updated so they request the combined **Author and Distill** pass for:

- replies
- product copy
- documents
- issue triage

This is a Mirket skill and instruction change, not a change to an external project. The recorded initiative date is **November 9, 2026**. The implementation report is associated with **REF-ID: `conversation:01a1bb84-4822-7903-a68a-ab67584fa15c`**.

The Mirket **Distill** guidance supporting the combined pass was rewritten on **November 10, 2026** to make the agent do authorized work first, skip routine narration, lead with verified results, and reduce avoidable communication overhead. It provides enough reasoning to assess responses, report meaningful progress and blockers, directly challenge doubtful approaches with evidence and a recommendation, prefer short paragraphs while using lists or tables when useful, and include outcomes, relevant checks, and material limitations in completion reports. The compact guidance runs at SessionStart and on each user prompt, then turn-end guidance is integrated into Clean’s existing review pass without requesting another continuation; host guidance remains distinct from hard output or token enforcement. These revised Distill capabilities were later released in Mirket 0.3.0.

Mirket’s `CONTRIBUTING.md` requires skill guidance to be authored from Mirket’s own requirements and observed behavior, without using external skills, prompts, or workflow guides as authoring sources.

On **November 11, 2026**, the Mirket repository’s broader lifecycle work expanded the catalog to a candidate **0.4.0** release with exactly **25 native skills**. It added **Secure, Release, Migrate, Deploy, and Operate**, and updated skill handoffs, routing, global instruction sources, the website, and installation documentation.

The new Mirket skills establish distinct lifecycle ownership: **Secure** handles security and privacy, **Release** prepares versioned releases, **Deploy** rolls them out, **Migrate** changes persistent state, and **Operate** maintains service health and recovery. Focus also gained a shipped-outcome review branch. This broader review addressed a previously identified gap after implementation, where release, rollback, operations, and learning from actual product use lacked explicit owners.

## Current state

The implementation report says that **all 14 repository tests passed**, including the **synthetic hook check**. These results establish local test success for the recorded repository checks, but not live Author behavior.

The work was still in an incomplete delivery state when recorded:

- the implementation report initially recorded the changes as **uncommitted**;
- the changes were **not installed** into the active Mirket plugin; and
- **live skill behavior remained untested**.

Therefore, the implementation report describes an initially uncommitted state. The available facts do not establish that the Author skill was installed into the active plugin or validated through live skill execution.

The recorded state still says that live Author behavior had not been tested; no later fact records that evaluation as completed.

A later Mirket-wide report says that all 56 Mirket tests passed. This broader test result does not establish that the revised Author behavior was installed or validated through live skill execution; the recorded Author-specific live evaluation remains unconfirmed.

As of **November 11, 2026**, the Mirket working tree was dirty while source manifests identified candidate version **0.4.0** and the 25-skill catalog; source instructions, routing, the website, and installation documentation had been updated. These facts do not establish a commit, publication, production deployment, or installation of the revised Author skill into the active plugin. The Author-specific live evaluation therefore remains unconfirmed.

It reports concise factual progress, meaningful blockers, and verified final outcomes; challenges concerns with evidence and a recommendation; includes relevant checks, reasoning, and material limits for technical outcomes; and prefers short paragraphs with lists or tables when useful. Host guidance remains distinct from hard output or token enforcement, and actual token savings have not been measured.

In the nazmirket project, the Mirket skills catalog initiative created and renamed the catalog namespace to "mirket" and shipped the native Mirket catalog, local workspace rules, and a marketplace with remote setup and an icon on November 9, 2026. The Mirket project expanded the catalog to address a product-development coverage gap after implementation: release and rollback, operations and recovery, and learning from actual product use previously had no explicit owner. The new ownership boundaries assign Secure to security and privacy, Release to versioned releases, Migrate to persistent-state changes, Deploy to rollout, and Operate to service health and recovery; Focus also gained a shipped-outcome review branch.

Mirket's memory-reliability work requires preserving existing working-tree revisions while fixing memory-configuration preservation, canonical-bank migration, effective diagnostics, and explicit freshness and recovery checks. Validation must cover the package, installed guidance, and host behavior without claiming instantaneous memory consistency; these constraints remain part of the initiative's verification requirements.

body:
The **Mirket Critique** initiative is revising the repository’s Critique skill so it can apply quality judgment at the right points in implementation and delivery, use evidence rather than unsupported claims, involve the human when product direction is at stake, and make only authorized corrections. The memory records that the skill was revised. The memory does not record a Critique-specific live-evaluation result.

## Project and scope

The initiative belongs to the **Mirket** repository and concerns the Critique skill at `plugins/mirket/skills/critique/SKILL.md`. The skill is intended to assess work **“during implementation when useful and before delivery when quality needs judgment.”**

The change is not a general audit of every project or repository. It is a focused revision of Mirket’s quality-assessment workflow: Critique should choose only the review lenses that matter for the task and its risks, then assess the relevant quality dimensions before or during delivery.

The Critique revision is part of the broader **Mirket repository** initiative authorized on November 11, 2026 and now represented in the working tree by a candidate 0.4.0 catalog of exactly 25 native skills. That initiative added Secure, Release, Migrate, Deploy, and Operate, extended existing skills, completed audit follow-up, and updated source instructions, routing, the website, and installation documentation. The accompanying repository review covers natively authored skills, skill wiring, guidance quality, coverage, hooks, Global Instructions enforcement, and simplification opportunities.

## What is being changed

The recorded initiative defines these changes:

- Use Critique **“during implementation and before delivery”** when quality judgment is useful.
- Select critique lenses based on the **task and risk**, rather than applying every possible review dimension indiscriminately.
- Require evidence for visual-quality claims. When no render can be inspected, visual quality must be reported as **“unverified.”**
- Require evidence for performance claims and state performance-evidence gaps while seeking a useful target or measurement.
- Distinguish quality findings from product-direction or taste concerns. Explain those concerns and involve the human when resolving them could materially change the outcome.
- Distinguish confirmed defects, supported risks, and material improvements in Mirket’s audit and lifecycle workflow, while preserving read-only defaults.
- Fix quality issues and recheck the result only **within existing authorization**; the skill is not meant to expand the authorized scope of work. This workflow also addresses lifecycle reliability and operational safety.

The consolidated description states that the revised skill will **“require evidence for visual and performance claims, involve the human in product choices, and correct and recheck quality issues only within existing authorization.”**

As a Mirket skill-redesign constraint, the Critique revision must preserve existing authored work, reconcile shared guidance, and show a visible baseline for the resulting skill.

## Why the change is being made

The purpose is to make Critique’s quality judgment useful throughout the work rather than limiting it to a final review. Reviewing during implementation can catch relevant issues while they are still actionable, while reviewing before delivery provides a final quality check when judgment is needed.

Choosing lenses by task and risk keeps the review proportionate and relevant. Requiring evidence prevents visual or performance conclusions from being presented as verified when the necessary render, target, or measurement is unavailable. Escalating material product-direction choices preserves human control over outcomes that are not merely technical quality defects. Restricting fixes to existing authorization prevents Critique from silently changing scope while still allowing it to correct and recheck issues it is already authorized to address.

## Current state

The memory says that **“The Mirket Critique skill was revised to implement its assessment, evidence, correction, and escalation workflow.”** The recorded revision therefore covers the intended workflow in `plugins/mirket/skills/critique/SKILL.md`.

The memory does not record a Critique-specific live evaluation, so the revised skill’s behavior in a live session remains **not recorded**.

As of November 11, 2026, the broader Mirket initiative has been implemented in the working tree as a candidate 0.4.0 catalog of exactly 25 native skills. The new lifecycle ownership is separated across Secure (security and privacy), Release (versioned release preparation), Deploy (rollout), Migrate (persistent-state changes), and Operate (service health and recovery); Focus also gained a shipped-outcome review branch. The website and documentation present the expanded catalog and a Release → Deploy → Operate → Focus lifecycle example. These broader repository changes provide context for the Critique revision but do not constitute a Critique-specific live evaluation.

- Fix quality issues and recheck the result only **within existing authorization**; the skill is not meant to expand the authorized scope of work. This workflow also addresses lifecycle reliability and operational safety.

The consolidated description states that the revised skill will **“require evidence for visual and performance claims, involve the human in product choices, and correct and recheck quality issues only within existing authorization.”**

As a Mirket skill-redesign constraint, the Critique revision must preserve existing authored work, reconcile shared guidance, and show a visible baseline for the resulting skill.

## Why the change is being made

The purpose is to make Critique’s quality judgment useful throughout the work rather than limiting it to a final review. Reviewing during implementation can catch relevant issues while they are still actionable, while reviewing before delivery provides a final quality check when judgment is needed.

Choosing lenses by task and risk keeps the review proportionate and relevant. Requiring evidence prevents visual or performance conclusions from being presented as verified when the necessary render, target, or measurement is unavailable. Escalating material product-direction choices preserves human control over outcomes that are not merely technical quality defects. Restricting fixes to existing authorization prevents Critique from silently changing scope while still allowing it to correct and recheck issues it is already authorized to address.

description: Summarize the "Revise Mirket Distill skill" initiative: what is being built or changed and why, and its current state — drawn from the project's memory. body:
The Mirket repository is revising its cross-cutting skills: Distill now favors authorized action, verified results, concise factual communication, and focused reasoning to reduce avoidable narration; its turn-end guidance is integrated into Clean’s existing review pass without requesting another continuation. Related routing and lifecycle-hook hardening makes ownership and commit targets more deterministic, keeps extra final review opt-in, and strengthens host and architecture checks. Clean continues to support safer cleanup. The current working tree contains a 0.4.0 candidate with 25 native skills, including five newly defined lifecycle and security responsibilities; source guidance, routing, website, and installation documentation were updated, but the candidate is not claimed as committed, published, deployed, or live-evaluated.

### Mirket Distill initiative

In the Mirket repository, Distill is being revised to have the target agent do authorized work before routine narration, lead with verified results, and report concise factual progress, meaningful blockers, and final outcomes. The purpose is to improve execution focus and reduce avoidable communication overhead.

Mirket's revised Distill applies compact guidance at SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit, then reinforces it at Stop within the existing single Clean continuation without requesting another continuation, while preserving existing prompt-hook behavior. The cleanup hook is Stop-neutral by default; with `MIRKET_FINAL_REVIEW=1` and `stop_hook_active` false, it can request one continuation. Host guidance remains distinct from hard output or token enforcement.

The Mirket Distill initiative's live evaluation remains deferred.

The Mirket Distill skill reports technical outcomes with relevant checks and material limits, directly challenges concerns with evidence and a recommendation, and includes enough reasoning for answers to be assessed. It favors short paragraphs, using lists or tables when useful.

In the Mirket repository, related routing and lifecycle-hook hardening makes commit targets deterministic, keeps read-only previews read-only, makes extra final review opt-in, surfaces one owner for each outcome, excludes read-only audits from execution plans, and permits bounded root integration fixes. It is intended to implement the Astra reviewers' findings and improve routing, lifecycle, architecture documentation, and cross-host integration reliability.

The Mirket repository now emits the one-owner rule and the exact path to `plugins/mirket/references/Routing.md` from `plugins/mirket/hooks/distill.py` at SessionStart. Supporting skills return evidence to the owner responsible for the outcome, clarifying routing when several skills overlap.

As part of the Mirket repository's broader 0.4.0 candidate initiative, the catalog is being expanded to 25 native skills by adding Secure for security and privacy, Release for versioned release preparation, Deploy for rollout, Migrate for persistent-state changes, and Operate for service health and recovery. Existing skill handoffs and Focus's shipped-outcome review branch were updated to clarify lifecycle ownership; the documented lifecycle example is Release → Deploy → Operate → Focus.

### Constraints and current state

`UserPromptSubmit` emits context directing the agent to Distill and reminding it about Clean; the prompt hook can request that the agent apply Distill but cannot guarantee compliance. Stop cleanup can request one continuation through the host's `stop_hook_active` flag. These hooks depend on host support and hook trust; their live host behavior has not been verified, and they are not a complete shell parser or a security boundary.

Mirket is the repository's primary plugin offering. Its distribution includes portable and Claude-specific plugin manifests, an icon, `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` files, Codex display metadata, shared references, and attribution notices.

In the Mirket repository, Distill and Clean are cross-cutting skills rather than individual stages in the workflow diagram. Mirket's routing is clarified in `plugins/mirket/references/routing.md` and skill trigger descriptions: `pick-skills` selects the relevant skillset on every prompt, while the workflows span project understanding, planning, engineering quality, design, communication, and coordination.

The Mirket Distill revision's live evaluation remains deferred. The catalog expansion is now represented in the working-tree 0.4.0 candidate with 25 native skills, while the related authored skill, routing, installation, website, and documentation changes remain candidate work rather than a claim of publication or deployment.

The 0.2.1 release's setup, static website build, and browser smoke checks also passed.

The Mirket repository's hardening work includes creating the first architecture decision record under `docs/decisions/` when no existing convention is available, adding host-contract regression tests, and creating a cross-host smoke matrix. The working-tree changes were uncommitted and not deployed or installed; live activation, released behavior, semantic routing, and live-host state remain unverified.

Astra High's review of the Mirket repository found that both existing test suites passed. A focused check reproduced a false commit block when a quoted `|` was treated as a shell operator; the November 10 revisions addressed the related hook, routing, approval, and handoff findings. A later audit recorded findings only and made no repository source or persistent configuration changes.

### Mirket skills website project

The Mirket repository also generates static versions of the workflow diagrams for the README.

For the Mirket repository's expanded 25-skill catalog, the website generates skill documentation and adjacent-skill navigation, with 28 documented indexable pages. It also provides source-aware Markdown links, responsive animated workflow diagrams with reduced-motion static presentation, and canonical metadata and discoverability artifacts; the website and documentation were updated as part of the candidate initiative.

body:
The **Mirket repository** initiative revises the Orchestrate skill so delegation is useful without giving up root-agent control, risk-appropriate verification, explicit approval boundaries, or independent review. The root is the sole delegator; workers cannot create or manage further subagents, and bounded root integration is allowed after workers return ownership. The initiative also hardens Mirket routing, lifecycle hooks, architecture documentation, and cross-host integration reliability. The working tree now describes a candidate 0.4.0 catalog with exactly 25 native skills, including Secure, Release, Migrate, Deploy, and Operate, but the latest hardening and catalog changes remain uncommitted and undeployed. The available memory still does not record a separate Orchestrate-specific live skill-test result.

## Project and scope

This initiative belongs to **Mirket**, specifically the repository files `plugins/mirket/skills/orchestrate/SKILL.md` and `README`. It was initiated on **November 9, 2026**, from the user's interactive decisions about how Mirket Orchestrate should coordinate work.

The intended change is to make Orchestrate a root-managed workflow:

- **Delegate when useful.** Delegation is an option, not an unconditional requirement.
- **The root alone delegates and manages delegated work.** Workers perform implementation and integration; the root coordinates the work and remains responsible for inspecting the results and evidence.
- **Use a plan gate for substantial implementation.** The related Mirket Plan decision says Plan should trigger for “substantial work or explicit planning requests,” and Orchestrate should align its plan gate with that rule.
- **Match model capability and cost to the work.** Use capable lower-cost models for “confidently deterministic tasks”; use strong models with generous reasoning and risk awareness for creative work or work with greater uncertainty and risk.
- **Inspect results according to risk.** The root must inspect delegated results and their evidence before accepting them. The root's own inspection does not count as independent review when a separate reviewer is required.
- **Assign corrections to workers.** Defective or incomplete delegated work is sent back to a worker or reassigned, then checked again by the root.
- **Continue inline only when delegation is unavailable.** Orchestrate should disclose that it is continuing inline, and inline execution must not be described as independent review.
- **Keep independent-review requirements explicit.** For substantial work, the workflow should request independent review, report when a reviewer is unavailable, and identify any unmet review requirement rather than presenting a self-check as independent.

Related **Mirket repository** workflow context is skill-based: `resolve-intent` clarifies the request, `plan` creates persistent explicit plans, `review-plan` spawns an independent reviewer, `delegate` assigns subagents with task-appropriate reasoning effort, and `get-feedback` requires user feedback on partial implementations before completion. A related routing rule records that Brief and Orchestrate pause only for assignment-relevant discrepancies.

A Mirket skill-redesign constraint is to preserve existing authored work, reconcile shared guidance, and make the prior baseline visible while revising Orchestrate.

A subsequent **Mirket repository/project** hardening initiative extends the routing and lifecycle work by making commit targets deterministic, keeping `git commit --dry-run` previews read-only, excluding read-only audits from execution plans, making the extra final review opt-in, surfacing one owner for each outcome, and simplifying bounded integration handoffs. The root remains the sole delegator, workers return ownership before bounded root integration, and subagents cannot create or manage further subagents. It also respects existing ADR conventions; when no convention exists, it initializes `docs/decisions` for the first settled architecture decision, adds host-contract regressions, and creates a cross-host smoke matrix.

## Authorization and plan behavior

A later Mirket repository guidance update clarifies the relationship between execution authorization and written-plan approval:

- Substantial implementation normally requires using Plan, resolving material decisions, and confirming authorization to execute.
- Plan uses the three `.work` plan records for substantial work, while allowing compact plans for small work.
- Clear existing authorization to execute remains valid; it does **not** mean that an unapproved written plan is approved.
- Stronger approval gates still apply when the user asks for a plan or when approval is otherwise required.
- During execution, Plan should ask about changes to outcomes, product decisions, or authorized scope.
- The Plan revision preserves the three `.work` plan records and avoids needless confirmation of unrelated established business rules.

Thus, the Orchestrate plan gate is intended to enforce planning and the appropriate approval boundary without incorrectly blocking work that already has clear execution authorization or treating that authorization as written-plan approval.

## Why the initiative exists

The purpose is to define safer and more predictable orchestration behavior for Mirket's root agent and workers. The decisions address several failure modes at once: uncontrolled delegation, accepting worker output without risk-based checking, using an unsuitable model for the task, silently falling back to inline work, losing the distinction between self-checking and independent review, and confusing authorization to execute with approval of a written plan.

The initiative also preserves human control over consequential decisions. Existing Mirket guidance says unresolved material decisions should remain visible rather than being silently settled by delegation, and the Orchestrate workflow must disclose gaps when an independent reviewer or delegation capability is unavailable.

The routing and lifecycle hardening is intended to implement findings from the two Astra reviewers and strengthen routing correctness, lifecycle behavior, architecture documentation, and cross-host integration reliability. Deterministic commit targets, explicit ownership, bounded handoffs, and targeted regression and smoke coverage reduce ambiguity and integration failures without making the extra final review mandatory in every case.

## Current implementation state

For the **Mirket repository**, the agent reported updating `plugins/mirket/skills/orchestrate/SKILL.md` and the repository `README` with the delegation, model-selection, risk-based review, correction, inline-fallback, and independent-review rules.

An earlier local-status report recorded that live skill testing had been deferred and the changes were uncommitted in the working tree.

A later Mirket status note says live evaluation of the remaining skills was deferred until the catalog was ready. The available records still do not establish a separate Orchestrate-specific live skill-test result beyond the repository tests and release validation.

The agent also reviewed Mirket's `plugins/mirket/skills/plan/SKILL.md` and aligned Orchestrate and the routing guidance with the execution-authorization rule.

The latest recorded **Mirket repository** initiative implements the two Astra reviewers' findings through deterministic commit targets, read-only Git previews, opt-in extra final review, one-owner routing, exclusion of read-only audits from execution plans, bounded root integration after workers hand ownership back, architecture documentation, host-contract regressions, and a cross-host smoke matrix. The first ADR was created under `docs/decisions/`. These changes were recorded as uncommitted and undeployed, so the record does not establish that the hardening work is complete or released.

The repository review examined natively authored skills, skill wiring, guidance quality, lifecycle coverage, hooks, Global Instructions enforcement, and simplification opportunities. Repository audits are expected to distinguish pre-existing working-tree changes from released or installed state.

As of November 11, 2026, the **Mirket repository** working tree identifies candidate version **0.4.0** with exactly **25 native skills**, adding Secure, Release, Migrate, Deploy, and Operate. The related skill handoffs, global-instruction sources, routing, website, installation documentation, and distribution manifests were updated; this is a working-tree state, not evidence of commit, publication, or production deployment.

The **Mirket repository** review recorded that both existing test suites passed. A focused check reproduced a false commit block when a quoted `|` was treated as a shell operator; the November 10 revisions addressed the related lifecycle-hook, routing, approval, and handoff findings through a trusted Git probe for staged-index checks, preservation of quoted commit arguments, corrected Design and Imagine routing, narrower approval and handoff gates, and simpler routine replies and small plans.

## Source attribution

All substantive facts above are attributed to the **Mirket repository/project** and its recorded user-agent decisions. The implementation report carries **REF-ID `conversation:01a1bb84-4822-7903-a68a-ab67584fa15c`**; the November 11 catalog and lifecycle updates carry **REF-ID `conversation:01a1c9a5-1c5c-7731-9a91-262b7402b72e`**.

- **Use a plan gate for substantial implementation.** The related Mirket Plan decision says Plan should trigger for “substantial work or explicit planning requests,” and Orchestrate should align its plan gate with that rule.
- **Match model capability and cost to the work.** Use capable lower-cost models for “confidently deterministic tasks”; use strong models with generous reasoning and risk awareness for creative work or work with greater uncertainty and risk.
- **Inspect results according to risk.** The root must inspect delegated results and their evidence before accepting them. The root's own inspection does not count as independent review when a separate reviewer is required.
- **Assign corrections to workers.** Defective or incomplete delegated work is sent back to a worker or reassigned, then checked again by the root.
- **Continue inline only when delegation is unavailable.** Orchestrate should disclose that it is continuing inline, and inline execution must not be described as independent review.
- **Keep independent-review requirements explicit.** For substantial work, the workflow should request independent review, report when a reviewer is unavailable, and identify any unmet review requirement rather than presenting a self-check as independent.

Related **Mirket repository** workflow context is skill-based: `resolve-intent` clarifies the request, `plan` creates persistent explicit plans, `review-plan` spawns an independent reviewer, `delegate` assigns subagents with task-appropriate reasoning effort, and `get-feedback` requires user feedback on partial implementations before completion. A related routing rule records that Brief and Orchestrate pause only for assignment-relevant discrepancies.

A Mirket skill-redesign constraint is to preserve existing authored work, reconcile shared guidance, and make the prior baseline visible while revising Orchestrate.

A subsequent **Mirket repository/project** hardening initiative extends the routing and lifecycle work by making commit targets deterministic, keeping `git commit --dry-run` previews read-only, excluding read-only audits from execution plans, making the extra final review opt-in, surfacing one owner for each outcome, and simplifying bounded integration handoffs. The root remains the sole delegator, workers return ownership before bounded root integration, and subagents cannot create or manage further subagents. It also respects existing ADR conventions; when no convention exists, it initializes `docs/decisions` for the first settled architecture decision, adds host-contract regressions, and creates a cross-host smoke matrix.

A later Mirket repository guidance update clarifies the relationship between execution authorization and written-plan approval:

- Substantial implementation normally requires using Plan, resolving material decisions, and confirming authorization to execute.
- Plan uses the three `.work` plan records for substantial work, while allowing compact plans for small work.
- Clear existing authorization to execute remains valid; it does **not** mean that an unapproved written plan is approved.
- Stronger approval gates still apply when the user asks for a plan or when approval is otherwise required.
- During execution, Plan should ask about changes to outcomes, product decisions, or authorized scope.
- The Plan revision preserves the three `.work` plan records and avoids needless confirmation of unrelated established business rules.

Thus, the Orchestrate plan gate is intended to enforce planning and the appropriate approval boundary without incorrectly blocking work that already has clear execution authorization or treating that authorization as written-plan approval.

## Why the initiative exists

The purpose is to define safer and more predictable orchestration behavior for Mirket's root agent and workers. The initiative also preserves human control over consequential decisions. The routing and lifecycle hardening is intended to implement findings from the two Astra reviewers and strengthen routing correctness, lifecycle behavior, architecture documentation, and cross-host integration reliability. Deterministic commit targets, explicit ownership, bounded handoffs, and targeted regression and smoke coverage reduce ambiguity and integration failures without making the extra final review mandatory in every case.

An earlier local-status report recorded that live skill testing had been deferred and the changes were uncommitted in the working tree.

A later Mirket status note says live evaluation of the remaining skills was deferred until the catalog was ready. The available records still do not establish a separate Orchestrate-specific live skill-test result beyond the repository tests and release validation.

The agent also reviewed Mirket's `plugins/mirket/skills/plan/SKILL.md` and aligned Orchestrate and the routing guidance with the execution-authorization rule.

The first ADR was created under `docs/decisions/`. These changes were recorded as uncommitted and undeployed, so the record does not establish that the hardening work is complete or released.

The repository review examined natively authored skills, skill wiring, guidance quality, lifecycle coverage, hooks, Global Instructions enforcement, and simplification opportunities. Repository audits are expected to distinguish pre-existing working-tree changes from released or installed state.

The November 9, 2026 revision is intended to make planning apply consistently to substantial work and explicit planning requests, while preserving existing `.work` plan records, avoiding unnecessary re-confirmation of business rules that the requested change does not affect, and distinguishing execution authorization from approval of a written plan. For substantial work, Plan uses three files; smaller work may use a compact plan. Live host and routing validation for the Plan initiative remained incomplete. On November 10, the **Astra Mirket audit follow-up** received approval for a sequenced implementation plan; on November 11, that audit recorded findings but no repository-source or persistent-configuration changes. Separately, the Mirket working tree’s source plugin manifests identify candidate version 0.4.0 with exactly 25 native skills, and source instructions, routing, website, and installation documentation were updated; the tree is dirty, and this is not evidence of a commit, publication, production deployment, or implementation of the Plan skill itself.

## Mirket Plan skill

### What is being changed

The Mirket Plan skill is being revised to:

- Trigger for **substantial work** or for **explicit planning requests**. Here, substantial work means work with consequential risk, unresolved decisions, or multiple dependent stages.
- Preserve the existing `.work` plan records and the tracking branch.
- Retain **unrelated established business rules without needless confirmation**.
- Record **routine technical adjustments**.
- Ask about changes to **outcomes, product decisions, or authorized scope** during execution.
- Request an **independent review** and disclose when that review is unavailable.
- Honor **clear prior execution authorization**, while distinguishing that authorization from approval of a written plan.
- Align **Orchestrate’s plan gate and the routing guide** with these Plan rules.

These are the intended planning and authorization behaviors recorded for the Mirket project on **November 9, 2026 at 20:22**.

For substantial work it uses three files, while smaller work may use a compact plan; this complements the revision’s preservation of existing `.work` plan records and its independent-review requirement.

### Why it is being changed

The rationale is to make the boundary between planning, authorization, and execution explicit:

- Planning should be required when the work is substantial or the user explicitly asks for a plan, rather than being applied indiscriminately.
- Existing business rules should not be reconfirmed when they are unrelated to the requested change; confirmation is relevant when the change affects a rule or when the intended behavior is genuinely unclear.
- A user’s clear authorization to execute should be respected, but a written plan should not be treated as approved merely because it exists.
- Changes to outcomes, product decisions, or authorized scope require attention during execution because they can alter what was originally authorized.
- Independent review must remain distinguishable from the agent’s own self-check, and an unavailable reviewer must be disclosed rather than silently treated as present.

The broader Mirket skill-redesign approach also requires preserving existing authored work, reconciling shared guidance, and showing a visible baseline; these principles reinforce the Plan revision’s preservation and alignment requirements.

The broader Mirket project’s November 11, 2026 working tree has source plugin manifests identifying candidate version **0.4.0** with exactly 25 native skills, including Secure, Release, Migrate, Deploy, and Operate; existing skills are also extended, and source instructions, routing, website, and installation documentation were updated.
